events.title: Python 3.14 released
events.summary: [Python] 3.14 shipped in October 2025 with further free-threading improvements, template string literals (t-strings), and deferred evaluation of annotations.
events.about: [Python] 3.14 continued the nogil path toward default free-threading in a future release, added t-strings for safer string templating, and simplified typing with lazy annotation evaluation. It keeps [Python]'s annual release train moving for web, data, and AI workloads.

narrative.whyChosen: 3.14 advanced the biggest architectural shift in [Python] since the 2→3 migration.
narrative.whyImportant: Free-threading and t-strings address parallel compute and injection risks in modern apps.
narrative.problemSolved: [Python] needed safer string interpolation and continued progress removing the GIL bottleneck.

events.title: Windows 10 end of support
events.summary: [Microsoft] ended free security updates for Windows 10 on October 14, 2025 — closing a decade-long [OS] generation still used on hundreds of millions of PCs.
events.about: Windows 10 EOL forced enterprises and consumers toward Windows 11 or paid Extended Security Updates. For developers it marked the end of targeting [IE]-mode legacy and an aging [kernel] baseline — one of the largest forced migration events in desktop computing since Windows XP.

narrative.whyChosen: Windows 10's EOL ended the longest-supported consumer Windows generation in years.
narrative.whyImportant: Hundreds of millions of machines needed migration or paid security patches.
narrative.problemSolved: [Microsoft] needed to sunset an [OS] generation to focus security engineering on Windows 11.
